onboarding.task.1.description:
Next Task recommends what deserves your attention. Capture what you need to do and open **Next** when you are ready to begin.

### How scoring works

The default formula combines:

- **Priority × 25:** each priority point adds 25 points.
- **Age in days × 0.25:** older tasks gradually gain attention.
- **Days since work × 1:** time since **Worked now** increases the score. Before the first work record, this counts from task creation.
- **Tag value × 20:** adds direct tags and their ancestors, counting each tag once. **Urgent**, with value 5, adds 100 points. Value 0 is for organization only.
- **Due date:** a future due date gains influence as it approaches. On the due date it adds 50 points, then another 20 for each overdue day. Without a due date, this part is zero.

The complete expression is:

```text
{formula}
```

In this expression, priority is the priority; ageDays, the age; idleDays, days since work; tagValue, the sum of tag values; hasDueDate indicates whether a due date exists; dueOffsetDays is the difference in days between today and the due date (negative before it is due). exp is the exponential function.

### When a task is marked as worked

Click **Worked now** after spending time on a task, even if it is unfinished. The app records the current date and time in **Last worked**. Starting a focus period with the task, blocking it, or restoring a block also updates this record. You can correct the date manually in Last worked.

**idleDays** starts over from zero, reducing the score contribution from time without work. Age and due date continue counting normally. The task stays pending until you finish or abandon it.

### How the next task is chosen

Among eligible tasks, the highest score is recommended first. Blocked, finished, or abandoned tasks are excluded. When unfinished subtasks exist, the app recommends a child action before its parent and may use the parent's score to prioritize it. Customize the formula in **Settings**.

These four examples use ordinary dependencies to introduce one step at a time. Use **Finish** to unlock the next example. **Abandon** also resolves dependencies without recording completion.
onboarding.task.1.title: Meet your next task
onboarding.task.2.description:
This task uses **Projects**, a child tag of **Work**. Applying a child tag also includes its ancestors.

Open **Tags** and change the value of Projects. Return to see this task's score. Use value 0 for tags you only need for organization. **Urgent** is a red root tag with value 5; combine tags across different topics.

Use **Finish** to unlock the due-date example.
onboarding.task.2.title: Try tags and their values
onboarding.task.3.description:
This example has a due date **7 days after your account was created**. As it approaches, its influence on the score increases.

Open the details and change or remove the date. For your real tasks, use a due date when there is a date commitment.

The previous task blocked this one: dependencies keep a due date from putting a step ahead of its prerequisite. Use **Finish** to unlock the last example.
onboarding.task.3.title: Try a task with a due date
onboarding.task.4.description:
Create your first real task: something small you need to do. Choose a tag and adjust its priority to your needs.

Finish this example and check the next recommendation. Use **Start focus** to work with the timer. All these examples are ordinary tasks: edit, finish, abandon, or delete them.
onboarding.task.4.title: Add something you do not want to forget
